newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria bids for early admission to NATO.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria bids for early admission to NATO.

text.p: Bulgaria said on Thursday its progress towards democracy, stable relations with neighbouring Balkan countries and the NATO-Russia security pact gave grounds to expect early admission into the alliance.

"Bulgaria expects its bid for full NATO membership to be considered due to its successful transformation to democracy and hopes to be among the first states to be invited to join the alliance," said the government in a declaration, which praised the NATO-Russia security pact signed on Tuesday in Paris.

The declaration coincides with a NATO decision announced earlier on Thursday to keep the alliance's doors open after it admits new members from the former communist east bloc at a summit in Madrid in July.

Foreign ministers gathered in the Portuguese town of Sintra to debate formally the most radical change in European security since World War Two said they would ask their leaders to make clear that enlargement was a continuing process.
NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana is expected to prepare by the end of June, a week before the Madrid summit, a shortlist of candidates and visit their capitals to inform them of the results.
Several NATO states expressed support for inviting as many as five new members into the alliance.

No countries were mentioned by name, but former Warsaw Pact members Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are favourites in the race of 11 contenders with Slovenia and Romania making strong late challenges.

"Bulgaria's merits are the success of democratic reforms over the past seven years and the good relations maintained between Bulgaria and its neighbouring countries," Deputy Foreign Minister Stefan Tafrov told reporters.
Bulgaria's interim cabinet in February made a clear statement of their desire to join NATO, and the new reformist government which took office last week reaffirmed this aim.
The Socialist government ousted from power by month-long street protests in January had always been ambivalent on NATO membership for fear of upsetting traditional allies in Moscow.
The declaration said the NATO-Russia security pact cleared the way for the alliance's eastward expansion and improved Bulgaria's prospects for joining the alliance.
